newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei tumbles after key supports broken.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei tumbles after key supports broken.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures took a heavy beating on Monday, tumbling after key supports were broken to end lower, dealers said.
Dealers said the Nikkei 225 December contract melted down after its support at 21,020 was broken and stops triggered. It proceeded to break supports at 20,940, 20,920 and 20,760.
December ended 405 points down at 20,720 on 17,000 lots. March shed 440 points to end at 20,725 on 6,160 lots.
Dealers said Bank of Japan's (BOJ's) governor Yasuo Matsushita's news conference caused a bit of a flurry.

Matsushita had said on Monday the central bank's easy money policy was intended to prevent a deflationary spiral, to strengthen corporate confidence and to put the economy back on a self-sustainable recovery track. He added that the first two aims had "just about been achieved".
"Earlier it was not clear which one of the three aims has not been achieved and that spooked the market," a dealer with a European institution said.
"By the time the market realised the third implied was the self-sustaining receovery, (bearish) technicals had already taken over," he added.
Dealers looked for the December Nikkei to next test 20,510 and 20,410, the acid test for Nikkei's sustainability.
